page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance allocates 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is capped at 8.0 GB, establishing a lean 1:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation of 1.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector acceleration is supported through AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI instructions, alongside AES cryptography extensions. The instance includes 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated GPUs, and supplies no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for non-volatile file operations.

Benchmark results reflect a low compute baseline compared against modern hardware tiers. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 996.0 and a multi-core score of 3814.0, accompanied by a PassMark CPU score of 7018.44. In synthetic multi-threaded workloads, stress-ng produced 5887.4, while PassMark database operations scored 2218.35. Memory throughput registered at 39.9 GB/sec for large block uncached reads and 32.58 GB/sec for uncached writes. For language model evaluation, CPU-based execution yielded 116.45 tokens per second for generation on a small 135M model, dropping to 5.09 tokens per second on a 7B model.

Due to the 1:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio and older CPU architecture, the ecs.ic5.2xlarge offers an economical footprint for applications constrained by CPU core counts rather than RAM capacity. It is primarily fit for lightweight web servers, moderate CI/CD build workers, queue processing, and microservices with minimal internal memory demands.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores and 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a tight 1.0 GB per core ratio. The configuration includes AVX-512 extensions, 2 Gbps baseline networking, zero GPUs, and no bundled local storage. In standardized benchmarks, the instance recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 3814.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 7018.44, alongside uncached memory read bandwidth of 39.9 GB/sec. Given its constrained memory density and entry-level benchmark scores relative to modern server architectures, this server functions best for low-memory CPU workloads, batch scripting, CI/CD runners, and light web front-ends.
